extracted.intended_audience: university founders, faculty, and Catholic educators (readers concerned with designing/defending a Catholic university curriculum)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and principles for what subjects a university should teach, how they relate to revealed religion, and the Church's role in secular education (lecture-form arguments aimed at shaping a Catholic university's curriculum and institutional character).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberal education subject-matter: Science and Literature
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three great subjects on which Human Reason employs itself:—God, Nature, and Man; and theology being put aside ... the physical and social worlds remain. These, when respectively subjected to Human Reason, form two books: the book of nature is called Science, the book of man is called Literature. Literature and Science, thus considered, nearly constitute the subject-matter of Liberal Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat liberal education as primarily the study of Science (nature) and Literature (man). Curriculum design should recognize these two as the staple mental exercises proper to a university and the central contents of the Faculty of Arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of Revealed Truth in a bona fide way
rubrics_metrics.description: If a University cannot fulfil its name and office without the recognition of Revealed Truth, the Church must be there to see that it is a bonâ fide recognition, sincerely made and consistently acted on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where theology/revealed religion is necessary to the university's identity, institutional arrangements must secure sincere, consistent recognition of Revelation rather than a nominal or adulterated acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mix methods: respect methodological boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: From religious investigations, as such, physics must be excluded, and from physical, as such, religion; and if we mix them, we shall spoil both. The theologian ... simply ignores the laws of nature; the physical philosopher ... is simply ascertaining those laws, putting aside the question of that Omnipotence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear methodological separation in teaching and inquiry: theology (deductive, revelation-based) and physical science (inductive, experiment-based) should be allowed their proper methods without inappropriate cross-application that would 'spoil both'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow Science but guard against anti-religious bias
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be no real collision between [physical science] and Catholicism. ... A vast multitude of its teachers ... have been either unbelievers or sceptics ... their emphatic silence or phlegmatic inadvertence as to [religion's] claims have implied ... that in their opinion it had no voice at all in the subject-matter which they had appropriated to themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach physical sciences fully (they deal with divine works), but be attentive to institutional culture and teaching that may implicitly exclude or dismiss religion; Church presence or oversight is recommended where necessary to prevent disproportionate secular/atheistic influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge Literature as the record of the natural (often sinful) man
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature stands related to Man as Science stands to Nature; it is his history. ... Literature is to man in some sort what autobiography is to the individual; it is his Life and Remains. ... Literature, as such, no matter of what nation, is the science or history, partly and at best of the natural man, partly of man in rebellion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum should present literature as the portrayal of human life (including moral imperfection). Expect and include works that reflect the natural (and sinful) condition of man rather than attempting to force a 'Christian' or sinless literature at the university level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not proscribe secular/classical literature from university study
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribe ... Secular Literature as such; cut out from your class books all broad manifestations of the natural man ... To-day a pupil, to-morrow a member of the great world: ... You have refused him the masters of human thought, who would in some sense have educated him ... Homer, Ariosto, Cervantes, Shakespeare ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should not exclude standard secular or classical authors because of incidental moral defects; students need exposure to the masters of human thought to be prepared for the world and to learn discrimination between 'the precious and the vile.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate curricula by audience — restraint acceptable for the young, not for university
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not say you cannot form a select literature for the young, nay, even for the middle or lower classes; this is another matter altogether: I am speaking of University Education, which implies an extended range of reading ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is permissible to curate gentler or selective reading for children/low-level instruction, but a university curriculum, by definition, must include wide and standard reading; do not shrink university reading lists to avoid engagement with challenging works.

rubrics_metrics.name: University education aims to prepare for worldly life
rubrics_metrics.description: For why do we educate, except to prepare for the world? ... If then a University is a direct preparation for this world, let it be what it professes. It is not a Convent, it is not a Seminary; it is a place to fit men of the world for the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design university programs to prepare students practically and intellectually for life in society; avoid treating universities as purely ecclesiastical or monastic institutions detached from worldly realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church's role: admission and purification rather than exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot feel any doubt myself ... that the Church’s true policy is not to aim at the exclusion of Literature from Secular Schools, but at her own admission into them. Let her do for Literature in one way what she does for Science in another; each has its imperfection, and she has her remedy for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Church should seek to participate in secular education — to purify and cultivate literature and science from within — rather than attempting to bar secular studies from educational institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use moral and attractive engagement (counter-fascination) in influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The mischief was to be met, not with argument, not with science, not with protests and warnings ... but by means of the great counter-fascination of purity and truth. ... He preferred to yield to the stream, and direct the current, which he could not stop, of science, literature, art, and fashion, and to sweeten and to sanctify what God had made very good and man had spoilt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional and pastoral responses to secular culture should include positive attraction (exemplary holiness, beauty, truth) and pastoral engagement rather than merely polemical argument or prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty of Arts (Arts/Letters) should be central to a university
rubrics_metrics.description: It is indeed not a little remarkable that ... a University, after all, should be formally based (as it really is), and should emphatically live in, the Faculty of Arts; but such is the deliberate decision of those who have most deeply and impartially considered the subject. Arts existed before other Faculties; the Masters of Arts were the ruling and directing body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the university structurally and pedagogically around the Faculty/School of Arts and Letters as the core from which other professional faculties grow and are balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mistake a curated Christian programme for genuine study of Man
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a contradiction in terms to attempt a sinless Literature of sinful man. ... You will have simply left the delineation of man, as such, and have substituted for it, as far as you have had any thing to substitute, that of man, as he is or might be, under certain special advantages. Give up the study of man, as such, if so it must be; but, say you do so. Do not say you are studying him, his history, his mind and his heart, when you are studying something else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the stated aim is to study human nature, curricula must include authentic representations of humanity, not only idealized or sanitized depictions; avoid pretending to study 'man' while presenting only an artificially perfected model.
